strings.d1.s0.name: Miradouro de Santa Luzia
strings.d1.s0.tips: Azulejo-tiled terrace with views of the Tejo and Alfama rooftops in the morning light.
strings.d1.s1.name: Castelo de São Jorge
strings.d1.s1.tips: Moorish castle with peacocks and 360° city views. Buy tickets online to skip the queue, then walk down through the streets of Alfama.
strings.d1.s2.name: Tasca do Chico Alfama
strings.d1.s2.tips: Sardines and bifana (pork sandwich); fado in the evening (no reservations, 20:00).
strings.d1.s3.name: Tram 28 Martim Moniz
strings.d1.s3.tips: The yellow tram runs from Graça to Estrela. Use a 24-hour card, watch out for pickpockets and board at Martim Moniz.
strings.d1.s4.name: Miradouro da Graça
strings.d1.s4.tips: Views of the castle and the bridge; a kiosk beer at sunset.
strings.d1.b0.name: A Baiuca Alfama
strings.d1.b0.tips: Tavern with amateur fado (vadio); ordering from the menu is compulsory.
strings.d1.b1.name: Panteão Nacional
strings.d1.b1.tips: White-domed pantheon with a terrace. An alternative to Alfama. On Tuesdays, the Feira da Ladra flea market.
strings.d2.s0.name: Mosteiro dos Jerónimos
strings.d2.s0.tips: A masterpiece of Manueline style; Vasco da Gama's tomb. Book a timed ticket online (the queue is 1 hour). Closed on Mondays.
strings.d2.s1.name: Pastéis de Belém
strings.d2.s1.tips: Bakery since 1837. Warm pastel de nata with cinnamon; the tiled rooms inside have no queue.
strings.d2.s2.name: Torre de Belém
strings.d2.s2.tips: UNESCO-listed river fortress, with the Monument to the Discoveries on the way. The outside is enough (the queue inside is 1 hour).
strings.d2.s3.name: MAAT Museum
strings.d2.s3.tips: Wavy museum on the riverbank; walk across the roof, with LX Factory opposite.
strings.d2.s4.name: LX Factory
strings.d2.s4.tips: Factory complex with the Ler Devagar bookshop and design shops; a market on Sundays.
strings.d2.b0.name: Rio Maravilha LX Factory
strings.d2.b0.tips: Rooftop bar with views of the bridge.
strings.d2.b1.name: Museu Nacional dos Coches
strings.d2.b1.tips: Royal carriages; an alternative to MAAT.
strings.d3.s0.name: Palácio da Pena
strings.d3.s0.tips: Take the train from Rossio (40 minutes, 2.45 EUR), then bus 434. A colourful, romantic palace. A timed online ticket is REQUIRED; first slot 09:30. The terrace is free but may be misty.
strings.d3.s1.name: Castelo dos Mouros
strings.d3.s1.tips: Moorish walls with views of Pena, 10 minutes on foot.
strings.d3.s2.name: Sintra Tarihi Merkez
strings.d3.s2.tips: Travesseiro (pastry pillow) and queijada (cheese tart) at Piriquita; the town square.
strings.d3.s3.name: Quinta da Regaleira
strings.d3.s3.tips: Masonic garden with the spiral Initiation Well and tunnels; empty at the end of the day.
strings.d3.s4.name: Sintra Tren Istasyonu Dönüş
strings.d3.s4.tips: Train back to Rossio; take bus 403 to Cabo da Roca (for sunset in summer).
strings.d3.b0.name: Palácio Nacional de Sintra
strings.d3.b0.tips: Royal palace with twin chimneys, in town; an alternative to Regaleira.
strings.d3.b1.name: Tascantiga Sintra
strings.d4.s0.name: Praça do Comércio
strings.d4.s0.tips: Square opening onto the river; terrace of the Rua Augusta Arch (4 EUR).
strings.d4.s1.name: Convento do Carmo
strings.d4.s1.tips: Gothic church whose roof collapsed in the 1755 earthquake; an open-air nave.
strings.d4.s2.name: A Brasileira Chiado
strings.d4.s2.tips: Pessoa's café: a bica (espresso) and a photo with the statue.
strings.d4.s3.name: Time Out Market Lisboa
strings.d4.s3.tips: Chef counters at Cais do Sodré; Manteigaria pastel de nata.
strings.d4.s4.name: Bairro Alto & Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara
strings.d4.s4.tips: A bohemian neighbourhood in the evening; terrace views and the bars of Pink Street.
strings.d4.b0.name: Cervejaria Ramiro
strings.d4.b0.tips: Legendary seafood beer hall; finish with prawns and a bifana. Expect a queue.
strings.d4.b1.name: Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga
strings.d4.b1.tips: Bosch's Temptation of St Anthony; an alternative to Time Out.
strings.d5.s0.name: Cascais Praia da Rainha
strings.d5.s0.tips: A winter walk along the seafront; the town.
strings.d5.s1.name: Boca do Inferno
strings.d5.s1.tips: The Hell's Mouth cliffs and crashing waves.
strings.d5.s2.name: Marisco na Praça Cascais
strings.d5.s2.tips: Seafood inside the market, priced by weight.
strings.d5.s3.name: Cabo da Roca
strings.d5.s3.tips: The westernmost point of Europe. Bus 403 takes 30 minutes; lighthouse, cliffs and wind.
strings.d5.s4.name: Praia do Guincho
strings.d5.s4.tips: Winter waves and a walk along the beach.
strings.d5.b0.name: Estoril Casino & Tamariz
strings.d5.b0.tips: Estoril beach and Europe's largest casino; an alternative to Cabo.
strings.d5.b1.name: Santini Cascais
strings.d6.s0.name: Museu Nacional do Azulejo
strings.d6.s0.tips: Tile museum with a 1738 panorama of Lisbon and a convent church.
strings.d6.s1.name: Oceanário de Lisboa
strings.d6.s1.tips: Europe's largest aquarium, on the Expo 98 site.
strings.d6.s2.name: Parque das Nações Nehir Kıyısı
strings.d6.s2.tips: The Vasco da Gama Bridge (17 km) and the cable car.
strings.d6.s3.name: Vasco da Gama Alışveriş Merkezi Yemek Katı
strings.d6.s3.tips: A quick lunch with river views.
strings.d6.s4.name: Mouraria & Martim Moniz
strings.d6.s4.tips: The immigrant neighbourhood where fado was born; Severa's house and street art.
strings.d6.b0.name: Zé da Mouraria
strings.d6.b0.tips: Giant portions of bacalhau (salt cod) in Mouraria; for lunch.
strings.d6.b1.name: Museu Calouste Gulbenkian
strings.d6.b1.tips: Lalique and Eastern art, plus a garden; an alternative to the aquarium.
strings.d7.s0.name: Cais do Sodré Feribot Cacilhas
strings.d7.s1.name: Cristo Rei
strings.d7.s1.tips: The brother of Rio's Christ; a lift takes you up 80 m for a panorama of Lisbon. Take bus 101.
strings.d7.s2.name: Ponto Final Cacilhas
strings.d7.s2.tips: Yellow tables on the riverbank; a farewell lunch with views of Lisbon. Reserve ahead.
strings.d7.s3.name: Aeroporto Metro
strings.d7.b0.name: Atira-te ao Rio Cacilhas
strings.d7.b1.name: Mercado da Ribeira Sabahı
strings.d7.b1.tips: Cais do Sodré market; an alternative to Cristo Rei.
strings.note0: The Viva Viagem 24-hour card costs 7 EUR (covers metro, trams and lifts; the Sintra/Cascais train is not included and costs 2.45 separately). Take the metro to the airport. The hills are steep; Bolt is cheap.
strings.note1: Winter is 10-15°C, rainy but with sunny days too. April-May is ideal; pastéis and fado all year round; Cascais is quiet in winter.
strings.note2: Pastel de nata 1.40, bica 1, bifana 4, restaurant meals 15-25. Send back the cover charge (bread/olives) if you don't want it. Tip by rounding up.
strings.note3: The Pena timed ticket is REQUIRED (online, morning 09:30); book Jerónimos online; most museums are closed on Mondays.
strings.note4: Pickpockets on Tram 28. The 'drug' dealers in Bairro Alto at night are fake, so ignore them.
strings.note5: Bacalhau (salt cod) has 365 recipes; sardines (June-August); ginjinha (sour cherry liqueur) 1.50 EUR at Rossio.
strings.transit.name: Viva Viagem / Navegante
strings.transit.why_chosen: 24 hours for 7 EUR on the metro, trams, buses, lifts and the Sintra/Cascais train
